JUDGMENT

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Inspector of Nandini Layout police station against the accused No.1 and 2 for the alleged C.C.28913/2021 offences punishable under Sections 498A r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
2.

In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that, the accused no.1 married C.W.1- Smt.Megha @
Meghalakshmi on 04.09.2020 as per Hindu rites and customs at Tamil Nadu and after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 and 2 at No.62,
K.S.C.B quarters, Coolie Nagar, Bengaluru, the accused No.1 and 2 with an intention Megha Alias Meghalakshmi vs Prabhakar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41251874/
1 to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention picked up quarrel with C.W.1 for petty reasons and harassed her for bringing additional as her parents had not given anything at the time of marriage, the C.W.1 unable to bear the harassment of the accused No.1 and 2 brought Rs.2,50,000/-as dowry from her parents and gave it to the accused.

Further the accused no.1 and 2 took the gold ornaments of C.W.1 and sold the jewelry and used the money and the accused No.1 and 2 harassed C.W.1 physically and mentally by demanding her to get additional dowry, therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused No.1 and 2 before the Nandini layout Police seeking necessary action against them in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No. 166/2021 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused No.1 and 2 , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, subsequently in persuance of summons the accused No.1 C.C.28913/2021 and 2 appeared before this Court and were enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused No.1 and 2 , therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 2 in the language known to them,
after understanding the same they denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5.
In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 11 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.
6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused.

7. In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-

sentences.text: 1. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that accused no.1 married C.W.1-Megha on 04.09.2020 and the accused No.1 and 2 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention after marriage demanded and received Rs.2,50,000/-, as dowry and and thereby the accused have committed an offence punishable under section 3 of D.P. Act?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was staying with the accused No.1 and 2 at the matrimonial house, at No.62, K.S.C.B quarters, Coolie Nagar, Bengaluru coming under jurisdiction of Nandini Layout P.s,
the accused No.1 and 2 with an intention to commit C.C.28913/2021 an offence and in furtherance of their common intention used to pick up quarrel with C.W1 for petty reasons and harassed C.W.1 physically and mentally by demanding her to get additional dowry and drove her out of the matrimonial house and thereby the accused No.1 and 2 have committed an offence punishable under section 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
3.

Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage also the accused No.1 and 2 have additional dowry and thereby the accused persons have committed the offence punishable under section 4 of D.P.Act?
4. What Order?

8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 3 : In the 'Negative' Point No.4 : As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Point No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.
10. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.

The C.W.1 being complainant as well as victim in this case is examined as P.W.1 and Ex.P.1 and 2 documents got marked on her behalf, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Megha and she deposed in her evidence that accused No.1 is her husband and accused no.2 is the mother in law and her marriage was solemnized with the accused No.1 on 04.09.2020 at TamilNadu.

Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused No.1 she was residing at the matrimonial house with the accused and they were living with together in cordial terms and the accused persons did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.
She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused persons.

She C.C.28913/2021 deposed that when she had been to Nandini Layout PS in the year 2021 police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and Megha Alias Meghalakshmi vs Prabhakar

on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41251874/
3 police did not draw any mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court, cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

11. As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses
, during the course of prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.

So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same, therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused No.1 and 2 however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 and 2 , for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 and 2 beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused No.1 and 2 , for which I answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the 'Negative'.
12. Point No.4:

In view of my findings on point Nos.1 to 3 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused No.1 and 2 are not found guilty and they are hereby C.C.28913/2021 acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused No.1 and 2 are ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
